transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27
Time: 15:00 UTC (approx 47 minutes)
Attendees: Nina Alvarez (Redwood AE), Jared Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Cerulean Head of ML), Ethan Park (Platform), Lola Reyes (PM)
Shared: demo deck https://redwood.ai/cerulean-deck, pilot scoping sheet https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/cerulean-pilot (note: proto link)

Summary/Topics (auto): prompt set composition, alerts for regressions, A/B split benchmarking, API/Console walkthrough, pilot scoping and security questions (SOC2, KMS, VPC)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Nina: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. I'm Nina from Redwood, AE for this region. With me is Jared, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:06] Maya: Hi Nina, good thanks. Excited to see how EvalOps could fit into our summarization flows.
[00:10] Ethan: Hi, Ethan here. I'll be thinking about infra and VPC constraints.
[00:13] Lola: Lola from product — keen to see A/B comparisons, how we'd measure user impact.
[00:18] Nina: Great. Quick agenda: show the Console demo for EvalOps, walk through prompt set design, then Jared will run a live split-bench and show regression alert configuration. Finish with pilot scoping and next steps. Sound good?
[00:27] Maya: Yep.

[01:05] Jared: Alright jumping in — I'm opening the Redwood Console. Forgive the latency, small share lag. So first, prompt sets. We typically recommend grouping by intent and label. For Cerulean's summarization use case, we'd create prompt sets for incident summaries, feature requests, and billing queries.
[01:24] Maya: Makes sense. We have around 30 intents, but for the pilot we want to start with the top 5 by volume.
[01:30] Jared: Perfect, that keeps signal high. In the Console you can upload a CSV of prompts and expected outputs — this becomes your evaluation corpus. We support structured expected outputs for classification or freeform text with similarity tolerances.
[01:42] Lola: Quick question — when you say similarity tolerances, is that cosine on embeddings or a token-level edit distance?
[01:48] Jared: Good question. We support both; by default for summarization we use a combination: ROUGE-ish metrics (string overlap) plus an embedding similarity threshold using our recommended base embedding model. The Console shows both metrics and you can set thresholds that trigger a regression alert.

[02:20] Maya: Are these metrics computed on each rollback? I mean, if we do a canary rollout how does it compare?
[02:25] Jared: Yes — you can define an experiment: split traffic 50/50 between model A and model B, and EvalOps will compute per-prompt pairwise comparisons. We do A/B comparisons with statistical significance checks, and you can configure how long or how many samples before we call a winner. There's also a pairwise report that surfaces prompts that disagree the most — that's great for root cause.

[03:10] Ethan: From infra side, our main constraint is that any PII prompt data must not leave our VPC unless it's encrypted. We're evaluating private deployment versus hosted. How does Redwood handle pilot telemetry?
[03:21] Nina: For pilots we can do two things: hosted with strict retention and KMS encryption, or Private deployment in your VPC. For the hosted pilot we can enable customer-managed KMS and SOC2 controls. If you need full air-gapped, we can arrange Private deployment — that'll be a separate engagement.
[03:40] Maya: Do you have an HSM or bring-your-own KMS flow?
[03:43] Jared: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS and HSM for key wrapping, and audit logs are available in the Console. I'll share the security pack after this call with specifics — it includes SAML/SSO, RBAC flows, and retention policies.

[04:12] Lola: Walk me through an example regression alert — what triggers it, and can we auto-roll back?
[04:18] Jared: Sure. You set a metric — e.g., mean similarity drop > 3% across top 1k prompts — and a window. If it trips, you can configure an alert to Slack/email and an automated policy to rollback the rollout. We also have tie-breaker rules: if latency increases but quality holds, you can prioritize cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:38] Maya: That tie-breaker sounds key for us — we care about both latency for live agents and cost for batch summaries.

[05:05] Jared: Demo time — I'm going to import a small mock prompt set (I've sanitized Cerulean examples). Loading... okay, prompts uploaded. Now I create an A/B split between two model versions — one is quantized Llama-variant, other is a higher-cost 8-bit float model.
[05:30] Nina: Note: model names in demo are placeholders, we can map to your enterprise catalog.
[05:33] Jared: Right. Running a split-bench now — this will run pairwise evaluations and produce a prompt-level delta heatmap. Results coming in...
[06:10] Jared: You'll see columns for similarity, hallucination score, and latency. For example prompt #12 shows the cheaper model has a 0.15 lower similarity and more hallucination tokens. We flag that as a regression candidate.
[06:28] Lola: Is hallucination scored via a detector you run or a human eval?
[06:33] Jared: It's hybrid — we have automated detectors (model-based) and you can plug in human labels. The Console surfaces both auto-detect and human feedback.

[07:05] Maya: What's the scale for the split-bench? Can it run on 10k prompts?
[07:09] Jared: Yes — for 10k prompts we recommend batching and a short window; runtime depends on model latencies. For hosted pilots we can run it in parallel across GPU pools. For private deployments we'll advise on capacity and can run a staged benchmark.

[08:00] Ethan: Network question — when you run bench for our private model, does KV cache ever get exported? We have concerns about caching artifacts.
[08:09] Jared: No KV cache is exported. For private, all execution and caches remain within the deployment boundary. In hosted mode, cache snapshots are encrypted and stored per-customer; we don't share across tenants. (transcription note: Jared said "K V cache" as separate sometimes)

[09:00] Jared: I'm switching to the alerts page. You can create a regression alert and attach a prompt set and primary metric. Alerts can be scoped per-route, per-model, or global. Also you can add a human-in-the-loop step before auto-rollbacks.
[09:20] Lola: For product we want the UI to show the top 10 prompts that drove the regression. Does Console do that?
[09:25] Jared: Yes — it surfaces delta-sorted lists and example diffs. You can link those back to the issue tracker via webhook.

[10:02] Maya: Are the metrics normalized for prompt length? Our summaries vary a lot in token count.
[10:09] Jared: We normalize by length for some metrics and provide per-length bucket breakdowns. There's a visualization for short/medium/long buckets. You can set different thresholds per bucket if needed.

[12:00] Jared: Now I'll show an A/B experiment report from a past customer. Note: names redacted. You get statistical significance, p-values, and a confidence interval. Console recommends sample size for a given delta.
[12:32] Lola: Can you tie experiments to user cohorts? e.g., internal agents vs weird external clients?
[12:37] Jared: Yes — experiments can be restricted by route or by metadata tags in requests. If you tag traffic at the SDK/API layer, Console will split and report by that tag.

[13:10] Ethan: On security, if we go hosted with customer-managed KMS, can we enforce zero-knowledge on logs? We need minimal PII in logs.
[13:20] Nina: You can configure redaction rules and retention windows. Also we support on-ingress redaction at the SDK layer so most PII never hits our logs. We'll provide the security checklist in the packet.

[14:05] Maya: How would you recommend we prioritize prompts for the pilot? We have volume and business-criticality metrics.
[14:12] Jared: Start with top volume intents + high-value intents (billing, safety). Also include known edge-case prompts where past models failed — that helps surface regressions quickly. For the pilot 2k prompts is a sweet spot.

[15:00] Jared: Running a live split now on a reduced set — showing the pairwise panel. You can see prompt-level diffs. For prompt 87 the cheaper model truncated important context — see the excerpt in the diff viewer.
[15:25] Lola: Can that diff viewer link to the original support ticket?
[15:28] Jared: Yep, we can link via metadata; Console will keep pointers.

[16:00] Maya: Pricing aside, what SLAs do you offer on pilot dedicated endpoints?
[16:06] Nina: For Dedicated we offer commit-backed throughput and SLA targets; for pilots we usually do a short-term dedicated slice with best-effort latency SLOs. We'll include pricing tiers in the pilot scoping doc.

[17:10] Jared: Quick note on cost controls — Console supports cost caps per-route and auto-fallback rules to cheaper models when a cost threshold is hit. Combined with EvalOps alerts you can do quality-first or cost-first policies.

[18:20] Ethan: If we want to run the pilot in our VPC, what's the typical lead time?
[18:25] Nina: For a VPC private deployment it's usually 4–6 weeks for the initial setup, depending on procurement and network approvals. Hosted pilot with KMS is faster — 1–2 weeks.

[19:00] Lola: For A/B comparisons, could we present results to non-technical stakeholders — like product or legal? How friendly is the export?
[19:07] Jared: We have exportable PDFs and CSVs; deck tiles you can drop into slides. Also a summary page with plain-English highlights.

[20:15] Maya: Any limitations we should know about with few-shot prompts — e.g. long context windows?
[20:22] Jared: We support variable sequence length profiling. If you're using long contexts, the runtime will select kernels optimized for that; the platform reports token breakdowns so you can trace cost vs context length.

[21:05] Jared: I'm going to seed a regression alert to show notification flow. Triggering... alert posted to Slack channel with prompt examples and a recommended rollback. (minor audio: small lag)
[21:40] Lola: Nice. Whoops, Maya — looks like one of our old demos triggered in the screenshot, ignore.

[23:00] Maya: A couple procurement/Qs: SOC2 type II is a must, we also need data residency in EU for certain customers. Are both supported?
[23:08] Nina: Yes SOC2 type II available; we have regional hosting in EU and can restrict data locality. For Private deployment, you control the region. I'll include the certs in the packet.

[24:30] Ethan: Network firewall rules — do you have a list of endpoints and port requirements?
[24:35] Jared: We'll provide a firewall spec. For hosted minimal, standard HTTPS endpoints. For private, additional control plane and health-check ports — I'll include in the packet.

[26:00] Lola: On success criteria for the pilot: Lola here — we want a clear pass/fail: e.g., no more than 2% drop in mean similarity across 2k prompts and latency under 250ms p95 for agent-facing routes. Can Redwood map those?
[26:12] Jared: Absolutely. We can codify that in the pilot scoping doc as acceptance criteria and configure automated checks.

[27:00] Nina: Let's talk timeline. Nina again: If we get the 2k prompts by 2026-03-03, SE runs a split-bench and returns results by 2026-03-05, and we review on a follow-up call on 2026-03-09 — does that work?
[27:15] Maya: That timeline is tight but doable.
[27:18] Ethan: Works for infra side if we get the firewall spec early.

[28:00] Jared: I'm going to annotate the split results with suggested threshold settings — e.g., set similarity alert at mean drop > 2.5% and per-prompt 0.2 delta. You can tune later.

[30:00] (Silence for a few seconds while Jared pulls up a sample exported report)

[31:10] Lola: I'd like the exported report to have the top 10 prompts where the models disagree and a human QA note field. Is that possible?
[31:16] Jared: Yes, we'll add a QA comment column and you can attach human labels.

[33:00] Maya: One more on evaluation: do you support multi-metric scoring, like combine similarity, toxicity, and hallucination into a composite score?
[33:10] Jared: Yes we support composite scoring and weighting. Console lets you weight metrics and will compute a combined score that you can threshold on.

[34:20] Ethan: For the pilot, we'd like to test both hosted-with-KMS and private on-prem options in parallel if possible — compare deployment costs and latencies. Feasible?
[34:30] Nina: It's feasible but increases complexity and cost. We can scope it in the pilot doc as an optional parallel track. Nina: we'll include cost estimates for both.

[36:00] Jared: Demo wrap-up — quick checklist: prompt set uploaded, split-bench ran, alert flow triggered, export generated. Sharing the PDF export now in chat.
[36:18] Nina: I'm dropping the pilot scoping sheet to the chat (link). Also security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack-cerulean (provisioned)

[37:00] Lola: Great. A few internal items: we need legal to look at the data processing addendum and a ballpark cost for a 3-month pilot.
[37:07] Nina: We'll include DPA and a pilot quote.

[38:30] Maya: Anything from your side we should watch out for? Known gotchas?
[38:35] Jared: Watch for label drift — if your label distribution changes over time you may see alert noise. We recommend periodic prompt set refreshes and human-in-the-loop sampling to recalibrate detectors. Also be explicit about which routes are in-scope for automated rollbacks.

[40:00] Ethan: One operational question: will the Console send detailed logs to our SIEM? We need to integrate with Splunk.
[40:07] Jared: Yes — we have log shipping integrations and webhooks. We'll provide the Splunk connector details in the security pack.

[42:00] Nina: Ok let's recap next steps: we will send the pilot scoping doc + pricing + security pack by 2026-02-28; Jared will run split-bench on Cerulean's 2k prompts after Maya shares them; follow-up call on 2026-03-09 to review results.
[42:18] Maya: Confirmed. 
[42:20] Lola: Confirmed.
[42:30] Ethan: Confirmed.

[43:00] (brief social)
[45:00] Nina: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email. If any urgent network/security items ping me directly.
[45:10] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
[45:15] Lola: Thanks all.
[45:20] Ethan: Bye.

[46:30] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had occasional speaker flips and mis-words (e.g., "K V cache" spacing). Some acronyms may be slightly off.
